entries.name: Easter
entries.capsule: Christian feast of the Resurrection, observed by Minnesota's many Catholic, Lutheran and other churches.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday after the first ecclesiastical full moon on or after March 21 (Western churches).
entries.whatItMarks: The Resurrection of Jesus in Western Christian tradition.

sources.title: Pew Research Center, Religious Landscape Study: Minnesota

entries.name: Christmas
entries.capsule: Christian feast of the Nativity and a Minnesota legal holiday on December 25.
entries.dateRule: December 25. When it falls on a Saturday the state holiday is the Friday before; on a Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus in Christian tradition; also a broadly observed cultural holiday.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 645.44 lists Christmas Day as a legal holiday on which no public business is transacted except in cases of necessity.

entries.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
entries.capsule: State and federal holiday honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., on the third Monday in January.
entries.dateRule: Third Monday in January (Minn. Stat. 645.44).

dates.source: Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated
Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated
Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated

entries.whatItMarks: The life and work of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: MPR News reported in 2012 that General Mills hosted an annual community breakfast for about 2,000 people at the Minneapolis Convention Center on the holiday; whether it continues was not confirmed.
entries.workplaceNote: Listed as a legal holiday in Minn. Stat. 645.44.

sources.title: MPR News, Newcomers say it's 'nice,' but not warm (2012)

entries.name: Juneteenth
entries.capsule: Marks the end of slavery in the United States; a Minnesota legal holiday on June 19.
entries.dateRule: June 19. When it falls on a Saturday the state holiday is the Friday before; on a Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.whatItMarks: June 19, 1865, when news of emancipation reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas; observed as a celebration of freedom.
entries.workplaceNote: Listed as a legal holiday in Minn. Stat. 645.44.

entries.name: Independence Day (United States)
entries.capsule: National holiday marking the 1776 Declaration of Independence; a Minnesota legal holiday.
entries.dateRule: July 4, with weekend shifts as set in Minn. Stat. 645.44.
entries.whatItMarks: The adoption of the Declaration of Independence, July 4, 1776.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026, the nation's 250th year, the Minnesota Historical Society displayed the state's two original constitutions through July 5 at the Minnesota History Center, timed to Statehood Day and the semiquincentennial.

minnesotaEvents.name: Display of Minnesota's two original constitutions

entries.workplaceNote: Listed as a legal holiday in Minn. Stat. 645.44.

sources.title: Minnesota Historical Society, Handwritten History Documenting Minnesota's Founding on Display

entries.name: Thanksgiving
entries.capsule: National harvest and family holiday on the fourth Thursday of November; state offices also close the following Friday.
entries.dateRule: Fourth Thursday in November (Minn. Stat. 645.44).

dates.source: Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated
Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated
Rule in Minn. Stat. 645.44; date calculated

entries.whatItMarks: A national day of thanks, usually observed with a family meal.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 645.44 makes the Friday after Thanksgiving a holiday for the state executive branch; other branches and local governments decide for themselves.

entries.name: Minnesota Statehood Day
entries.capsule: Anniversary of Minnesota's admission as the 32nd state on May 11, 1858.
entries.dateRule: May 11.

dates.source: Fixed anniversary stated by Minnesota Historical Society
Fixed anniversary stated by Minnesota Historical Society

entries.whatItMarks: Congress's approval of Minnesota statehood on May 11, 1858. KSTP, citing the Historical Society, says word reached Minnesota on May 13.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Not a legal holiday. In 2026 the Minnesota Historical Society displayed the two original state constitutions at the Minnesota History Center from May 6 to July 5, timed to Statehood Day.

minnesotaEvents.name: Display of Minnesota's two original constitutions

entries.name: Syttende Mai
entries.capsule: Norwegian Constitution Day, celebrated in Minnesota with festivals such as Spring Grove's, held the weekend nearest May 17.
entries.dateRule: May 17; Spring Grove's festival is the weekend nearest May 17, with a homecoming held instead every ten years.

dates.source: Fixed date; Spring Grove community calendar
Fixed date; Spring Grove community calendar

entries.whatItMarks: Norway's constitution of May 17, 1814.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Spring Grove holds a Syttende Mai festival with a parade and Norwegian food and crafts, supported by its Sons of Norway lodge; every ten years the town holds a homecoming instead. The organizer's next listed festival is May 17 to 21, 2028.

entries.name: George Floyd remembrance
entries.capsule: Anniversary of George Floyd's murder by a Minneapolis police officer on May 25, 2020, marked at George Floyd Square.
entries.dateRule: May 25 anniversary; organizers set events each year.

dates.source: KAAL report on the 2026 Rise and Remember festival

entries.whatItMarks: The killing of George Floyd at 38th Street and Chicago Avenue in Minneapolis on May 25, 2020, and the movement that followed.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The annual Rise and Remember festival at George Floyd Square offers music and art focused on healing and racial justice and ends with a candlelight vigil. Reconstruction of the square was set to begin June 8, 2026, and last two years.

sources.title: KAAL, George Floyd Square hosts annual festival six years after his death

entries.name: Rondo Days
entries.capsule: St. Paul festival honoring the historic Black Rondo neighborhood, divided by Interstate 94.
entries.dateRule: Set by organizers; traditionally a Saturday in mid-July.

dates.source: Seed calculation (third Saturday of July); not announced
Seed calculation (third Saturday of July); not announced

entries.whatItMarks: The history of St. Paul's Rondo neighborhood and the families displaced by I-94 construction between 1956 and 1968.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Begun in the 1980s; the 2026 festival at the Martin Luther King Jr. Recreation Center featured music, food trucks, art and sports.

minnesotaEvents.name: Rondo Days
minnesotaEvents.place: Martin Luther King Jr. Recreation Center, St. Paul

entries.name: Minnesota State Fair
entries.capsule: Twelve-day state fair ending on Labor Day, one of the largest in the world, in Falcon Heights.
entries.dateRule: Twelve days ending on Labor Day.
entries.whatItMarks: Minnesota agriculture, art and industry; held since 1859, growing out of an 1855 territorial fair.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: On 322 acres between Minneapolis and St. Paul, financially self-supporting since 1949. The 2026 fair counted 1,923,325 visits, its seventh-highest total. The fair publishes pages in Spanish, Hmong and Somali.

sources.title: Minnesota State Fair, About the Fair

entries.name: Saint Paul Winter Carnival
entries.capsule: St. Paul's annual winter festival, centered on the King Boreas Grande Day Parade.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Saint Paul Festival and Heritage Foundation; late January to early February.

dates.source: 2026 dates not found in an opened source

entries.whatItMarks: Winter in St. Paul.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Most events are free or low-cost, some requiring a carnival button; the King Boreas Grande Day Parade is the centerpiece.

entries.name: Governor's Fishing Opener
entries.capsule: Statewide opening weekend of walleye fishing season, marked since 1948 by a governor's event in a host town.
entries.dateRule: Opening weekend of the walleye season in May; the host town and dates are announced by the governor's office.
entries.whatItMarks: The start of the open-water fishing season; the walleye became the state fish on opening day in 1965.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The 78th Governor's Fishing Opener was held in Stillwater on the St. Croix River in 2026; the 79th is set for Cold Spring in 2027.

entries.name: Anoka Halloween
entries.capsule: Month-long Halloween festival in Anoka, which took the title 'Halloween Capital of the World' in 1937.
entries.dateRule: Events through October, ending on Halloween, October 31.
entries.whatItMarks: Halloween, and Anoka's century-old citywide celebration begun to discourage pranks.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Parades and events through October; the organizer called 2026 its 106th festival season.

minnesotaEvents.name: Anoka Halloween 2026 festival season
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: October 2026, with events on Oct. 30 and 31

entries.name: Grand Old Day
entries.capsule: Street festival on St. Paul's Grand Avenue on the first Sunday in June.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday in June.
entries.whatItMarks: Early summer on Grand Avenue.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Held 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Grand Avenue in 2026.

sources.title: Grand Avenue Business Association, Grand Old Day

entries.name: Twin Cities Pride Festival
entries.capsule: Free LGBTQ Pride festival in Minneapolis's Loring Park, which bills itself as Minnesota's second-largest festival.
entries.dateRule: Last full weekend of June, as announced by Twin Cities Pride.
entries.whatItMarks: LGBTQ pride and community.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Three stages and more than 650 vendors in Loring Park, with a Friday youth night.

sources.title: Minnesota Public Radio at Twin Cities Pride
Citizens for a Loring Park Community

entries.name: Twin Cities Marathon weekend
entries.capsule: October running weekend from Minneapolis to St. Paul.
entries.dateRule: First weekend of October, as announced by Twin Cities in Motion.
entries.whatItMarks: A community running festival.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: 5K, 10K and family events on Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026; 10 mile, half marathon and marathon on Sunday, Oct. 4.

entries.name: Annunciation shooting remembrance
entries.capsule: Remembers the Aug. 27, 2025, shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School in Minneapolis.
entries.dateRule: August 27, the anniversary of the 2025 shooting.
entries.whatItMarks: The mass shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School that killed two children and injured 29 others.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026 local elected officials hosted a day of service and remembrance at Pearl Park in Minneapolis, at the Annunciation community's request; Annunciation held private events.

minnesotaEvents.name: Day of Service and Remembrance
minnesotaEvents.place: Pearl Park and Annunciation Church, Minneapolis

entries.dateRule: Four days in July, set by the Minneapolis Downtown Council.
